definitions.explanation: A supernatural evil being or malevolent force. Common in religious, mythological, and fantasy contexts.
Supernatural or dark power, or the temptation to do something harmful. Used in compounds related to magic, witchcraft, and irresistible urges.

examples.english: I was seized by a moment of madness.

examples.japanese: {勇者|ゆうしゃ}が{魔王|まおう}を{倒|たお}す{物語|ものがたり}。
examples.english: A story of a hero defeating the demon king.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{普段|ふだん}は{真面目|まじめ}だが、{魔|ま}が{差|さ}して{嘘|うそ}をついてしまった。
examples.english: He's normally honest, but a moment of weakness made him tell a lie.

examples.japanese: {魔法|まほう}が{使|つか}えたらいいのに。
examples.english: I wish I could use magic.

examples.japanese: この{場所|ばしょ}には{魔|ま}の{力|ちから}が{宿|やど}っている。
examples.english: A dark power dwells in this place.

examples.japanese: {睡魔|すいま}に{襲|おそ}われて、{会議中|かいぎちゅう}なのに{目|め}が{閉|と}じそうになった。
examples.english: Drowsiness overcame me, and I nearly closed my eyes even though I was in a meeting.

notes:
Refers to demons, evil forces, and dark magic. Extremely productive in compounds. The expression {魔|ま}が{差|さ}す (literally 'the devil slipped in') is one of the most common everyday uses.

KEY EXPRESSION:
{魔|ま}が{差|さ}す — to be momentarily tempted; to act on a sudden impulse (usually to do something wrong). Used to explain uncharacteristic bad behavior.

COMPOUNDS:
- {魔王|まおう} — demon king
- {魔法|まほう} — magic, sorcery
- {魔女|まじょ} — witch
- {魔物|まもの} — demon, monster
- {魔力|まりょく} — magical power
- {悪魔|あくま} — devil, demon
- {睡魔|すいま} — drowsiness (literally 'sleep demon')
- {魔除|まよ}け — charm against evil, talisman

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {魔|ま}が{差|さ}す — to have a moment of weakness
- {魔|ま}の{手|て} — the clutches of evil
- {魔|ま}の{力|ちから} — demonic/dark power
- {魔|ま}の{時間帯|じかんたい} — the 'witching hour' (dangerous period)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {鬼|おに} — ogre, demon (more Japanese folklore, less supernatural evil)
- {悪魔|あくま} — devil (specifically the Devil or a demon in the Christian sense)
